title: Sanjay Gupta, Director of Kaante and Kaabil, Dies in Mumbai at 57
excerpt: The filmmaker behind a generation of stylised Hindi crime dramas died at home on October 30 after a fall, colleagues and police reports say. He is survived by his wife, Anu Lekhi.
body:
• Filmmaker Sanjay Gupta, director of Kaante, Shootout at Wadala and Kaabil, died at his Mumbai home on October 30, 2026. He was 57.
  • Sources told IANS he slipped in his bathroom at night and suffered a head injury; Versova police have registered an accidental death report and found no evidence of foul play so far, according to reports.
  • Filmmaker Ashoke Pandit confirmed the death on Instagram, and Milap Zaveri also confirmed the news, reports said.
  • Gupta is survived by his wife, Anu Lekhi. His last film was The Miranda Brothers, released in 2025.

Sanjay Gupta, the Hindi filmmaker whose glossy, hard-edged crime dramas defined a strain of Bollywood filmmaking in the 2000s, died at his Mumbai residence on October 30. He was 57. (The director is not related to the American neurosurgeon and broadcaster of the same name.)

Sources close to the family told IANS that Gupta slipped in his bathroom at night and injured his head. Reports said he was found the following morning. Versova police have registered an accidental death report, and the circumstances remain under investigation, with no evidence of foul play found so far, according to reports.

"It's really shocking and sad. Just got the news that our dear friend an ace director @_sanjaygupta is no more. He passed due to a head injury at home."

— Ashoke Pandit, filmmaker, on Instagram

Pandit added: "Another talent gone too soon. He was a wonderful narrator, full of life persona & a passionate filmmaker. A great loss to our industry." Filmmaker Milap Zaveri also confirmed the death, according to reports.

A career built on crime stories

Gupta stepped into cinema in 1994 with Aatish: Feel the Fire, starring Aditya Pancholi and Sanjay Dutt. He went on to direct, produce and write films including Ram Shastra, Khauff and Jung. His breakthrough came with Kaante in 2002, a heist film led by Amitabh Bachchan, Sanjay Dutt and Suniel Shetty. While filming Kaante in Los Angeles in 2001, the 9/11 attacks forced the production to relocate planned scenes from areas then considered sensitive, IANS reported.

Over a career spanning three decades, Gupta collaborated repeatedly with Sanjay Dutt, on films including Kaante, Musafir and Zinda — the last an unofficial remake of the South Korean film Oldboy. He produced Shootout at Lokhandwala (2007) and the anthology Dus Kahaniyaan, and directed and co-produced Shootout at Wadala (2013), the prequel to Lokhandwala. His later directorial work included Jazbaa (2015), Kaabil (2017) with Hrithik Roshan, and Mumbai Saga (2021).

Gupta became known for bringing a distinctive, stylised edge to Hindi crime dramas and action thrillers, and he frequently cast Sanjay Dutt and John Abraham across his films. For diaspora audiences, Kaante in particular travelled well: a heist film shot partly in Los Angeles, built around an ensemble of Bachchan, Dutt, Suniel Shetty, Mahesh Manjrekar, Lucky Ali and Kumar Gaurav, it remains one of the most recognised Hindi films of its decade.

His last film

Gupta's last work was The Miranda Brothers, released in 2025, which he directed and produced. The film, starring Harshvardhan Rane and Meezaan Jafri, followed an orphan rescued from trash who becomes devoted to his elder brother, both growing up to be star footballers until their mother's suspicious death threatens to tear them apart.

Details of his last rites were awaited. His filmography is catalogued on his Wikipedia page.
